qt: to the Council François Kalfon (S&D), Ştefan Muşoiu (S&D), Delara Burkhardt (S&D), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE) Subject:

The major oil companies have earned more than USD 460 billion in profits since the start of the war in Ukraine. They have also made more than USD 90 billion since the beginning of the war in Iran, due to soaring petrol prices. At the same time, Europeans’ fuel bills have skyrocketed. They now amount to up to EUR 300–EUR 400 for low-income workers, particularly nurses, and the self-employed. Thus, private profits are breaking records, and low-income households are once again the hardest hit. In August 2026, the German, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Austrian and Portuguese finance ministers formally called on the Council to introduce a tax on the oil companies’ windfall profits. Yet concrete measures are still lacking. Europe must act urgently to support lowincome households and radically accelerate the electrification of road transport. In light of the above: 1.
Will the Council introduce a European tax on the windfall profits of the major oil companies?
Will the Council earmark all the revenue from this tax to support low-income households and professionals commuting long distances, and to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels?
